material_definitions: The samples belong to the thio-LISICON solid solution system with the general formula Li4-xGe1-xPxS4.
They were synthesized using a standard solid-state reaction method involving Li2S, GeS2, and P2S5.
Ionic conductivity was measured using AC impedance spectroscopy across a broad temperature range.
The composition x=0.6 exhibited the highest ionic conductivity within this thio-LISICON series.
measurements.source_caption: Arrhenius plots of the ionic conductivity for various compositions in the Li4-xGe1-xPxS4 system.
warnings: Conductivity value estimated from the log scale on the Y-axis of the Arrhenius plot.

material_definitions: A systematic study of Li1+xMxTi2-x(PO4)3 with M=Al, Cr and Fe and 0 <= x <= 1 has been carried out by X-ray and neutron powder diffraction and by impedance spectroscopy.
The analysis describes the disposition of lithium atoms occupying M1 and a new M2' position.
The highest conductivity was found in the sample Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3.
Activation energy for bulk dc conductivity was measured at 0.30 eV.
The materials are solid solutions of the general formula Li1+xMxTi2−x(PO4)3 where M is Al, Cr, or Fe.
Samples were characterized by neutron powder diffraction and complex impedance spectroscopy to study crystal structure and ionic transport.
Ionic conductivity mechanisms were separated into bulk (dc) and grain boundary contributions across wide frequency and temperature ranges.
Substitution levels x range from 0 to 0.3, with conductivity generally increasing as substitution content increases.
